summary: Article card for community portals: a dark-gradient cover (code snippet or image), tags, clickable title, excerpt, author with avatar, date and reading time, and a reactions bar (likes, comments, bookmarks) that can be interactive.
whenToUse: Highlighting an article or community blog post (featured variant).
Listing articles in a grid of compact cards with author and reactions.
Reusing ReactionBar under an article or any content with likes and bookmarks.
whenNotToUse: Dense lists of voted posts: use PostList.
Discussion threads without excerpt or cover: use DiscussionList.
Generic content without author or reactions: use Card.

props.name: title
props.description: Article title; with href the whole card becomes clickable (stretched link).

props.name: variant
props.description: featured: cover beside the content (wide container) or above it (narrow); compact: no cover and tighter layout.

props.name: cover
props.description: Cover content (a code <pre>, an image). Featured variant only.

props.name: image
props.description: Article cover image. Replaces cover; use alt="" if decorative.

props.name: tags
props.description: Chips or Badges above the title.

props.name: author
props.description: Author: visible name and Avatar (image or initials).

props.name: date
props.description: Publication date: a Date becomes RelativeTime, anything else is shown as is.

props.name: readingMinutes
props.description: Reading time in minutes (“9 min read”).

props.name: likes / comments / bookmarks
props.description: Reaction counts, formatted with Intl (compact notation).

props.name: isLiked / onLike
props.description: With onLike, the like becomes a toggle button (aria-pressed).

props.name: isBookmarked / onBookmark
props.description: With onBookmark, the bookmark becomes a toggle button (aria-pressed).

props.name: commentsHref
props.description: Turns the comment count into a link.

props.name: ReactionBar.formatOptions
props.description: Count format when using ReactionBar on its own.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Renders a SkeletonCard of the same shape in its place (cover only in the featured variant), with aria-busy and hidden, non-live “Loading…” text, keeping className and style so it stays in the grid. Wrap the area in SkeletonGroup for a single announcement.

inherits: ArticleCard: HTML attributes of <article>. ReactionBar: HTML attributes of <div>.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the title link, then to interactive tags and reactions.
Opens the article from the title link.

accessibility: <article> element named by the title (aria-labelledby); the title is a heading of the chosen level.
The title link covers the whole card via a pseudo-element: a single tab stop, while tags and reactions stay on top and clickable.
Interactive like and bookmark are React Aria ToggleButtons with aria-pressed; the name includes label and count (“Likes: 412”).
Icons are decorative; static counts have their label in visually hidden text.
The avatar is decorative because the author's name is already visible.
In forced-colors mode the cover uses Canvas/CanvasText and the active reaction state uses Highlight.
responsive: Container query: above 40rem wide the cover sits beside the content, below it moves to the top.
Tags, metadata and reactions wrap; it stays usable at 320px.
Use Grid with minItemWidth for grids of compact cards.
customization: Tokens: --dc-look-radius-container, --dc-color-surface-inverse and --dc-color-text-inverse (cover, limited lightening via relative color), --dc-color-action-primary, --dc-color-accent-default and --dc-color-data-1…6 for the glows, --dc-color-accent-container for the active like.
commonMistakes: Putting links or buttons in the title: the whole card is already the link; use tags and reactions for other actions.
Passing isLiked without updating the likes count: the number shown always comes from props.
Using a cover with important text and no alternative: the cover is content like any other, so give images an alt.

limits: The count does not change on its own when toggled: update it in the parent (even in uncontrolled mode).
In browsers without relative color syntax the cover uses --dc-color-surface-inverse, which is light in the dark theme.
